notes: New: smart taxis in every speedwalk ('sp', map clicks, walk-there links). Each hail teaches where its destination drops you, and whether the room you hailed from works (outside), says 'go outside' (inside) or gets no answer (the wilds). When a speedwalk would be clearly shorter by walking to a known hail spot, hailing and walking the rest, it does that and tells you. It only hails from rooms where a taxi has come before, so it never wanders around trying. Arkania, Lorrd and Wroona are known from the recordings. 'taxis' shows what's known, 'taxis off' turns it off ('taxi' is still the game's shuttle command).

Trade and Auto Cargo now fly around closed hyperlanes. A lane known to be blocked (red on the Galaxy map: Ryloth - Lorrd and Arkania - Lorrd right now) is never suggested straight any more: the route goes via a system in between (Eeropha) and its distance, time and credits per hour count the longer way and the extra jump. A route with no way through at all isn't suggested. Auto Cargo makes the stop itself (jump to Eeropha, calculate again, jump on to the planet), and if a lane turns out to be blocked mid-run it notes it and takes the way around instead of stopping.

Each stop on a way around now says what it is: 'just passing through' when your fuel lasts to the end (you only drop out, calculate and jump on), or 'LAND and refuel at ...' when it won't (Eeropha's Refueling Outpost, or the planets in that system). You see it under the leg in Trade, in 'flight <planet>', and from Auto Cargo when it plans the jump. At a refuel stop Auto Cargo pauses with the reminder; land, refuel, launch, then 'autocargo resume' gets clear and jumps on. A refuel stop also counts in the route's time per loop.

Bank: a new look. Every account is its own row with real buttons (Deposit, Withdraw, Balance, From / To, Close; Close asks 'SURE?' first), the totals sit at the top (in the bank, on hand, at a bank), and quick amounts (10k, 100k, 1M, all cash on hand) fill the Amount box. History and known banks moved to their own tabs, so a deposit no longer pushes your accounts down the page.

Landing (Auto Cargo): any pad will do now, garages included (cargo trades there too), picked at random. Your own clan's pads come first (the safest; your clan is read from 'score'), other clans' pads only as a last resort. A pad that answers "Restricted Landing pad" is skipped for that character from then on, whoever sent the land. A planet whose pads aren't known yet gets a plain 'land <planet>' first to list them. 'pads <planet>' shows CLAN / ok / other / refused per pad.

New: Smart Exits. Doors you open with a command now work by walking: on Arkania's Mountainside Road just type 'se' and it pushes the palm for the city airlock; at Merr-Sonn's secured doors the direction says 'enter' / 'exit' for you. 15 doors from the recordings are built in (Arkania, Merr-Sonn, Kala'uun spaceport, Lorrd spaceport, Kafrene). A new door learns itself: open it once with say / push / press and walk through, and from then on the direction does it. Speedwalks and map clicks use them too. 'sx' lists a room's, 'sx se push palm' adds one, 'sx se remove' takes one out.

Fixed: the hyperlane lines and jump-range ring didn't show on the Galaxy tab (they were drawn behind the starfield). The untested grey lanes are brighter too, and lanes learned while another tab is open appear when you open the Galaxy tab.
Fixed: 'flight', the range ring and Ship Stats now know your ship after a restart while you're aboard (from the room you're in, and the last ship you boarded).

Ship Stats: type any number of units to add in the new box (1, 50, 1000...), or click +1 / +5 / +10 / +50 / +100 / +1000. Every row now counts real units (no more x10 / x100), and shows how many more of each fit in the ship's free quota.

New: Omi Flight. 'flight' shows your ship's real numbers, worked out from 83 recorded flights: a jump takes 500 x parsecs / hyperspeed seconds, fuel = the ship's fuel-per-parsec x parsecs (YT-1000 229, Flashfire 80), realspace speed / 10 units a second, and every Maneuver point under 100 adds half a second to launches, landings and turns. 'flight <planet>' = a jump from where you are: time, fuel, the whole leg. Help > Guides > Flight.

Getting clear to jump: after every launch the radar is read and, if another ship sits in your way, a course is set the fastest way to 500 units from everything. 'getclear' does it by hand (it speeds back up first if you were stopped).

TRACTOR BEAM alarm: the moment a ship locks on, Auto Cargo and the Fly Loop pause and STAY paused (a checkpoint, a pirate or an enemy: you decide). When it's sorted, 'autocargo resume' speeds back up and either gets clear and jumps again, or flies on to land.

New: hyperlanes on the Galaxy tab. White lines = lanes that work (a calculation went through, a jump was made, or the hyperlane monitor says Passable), red = blocked (interference, or No Route on the monitor), grey dashes = never tried but within your ship's range. A ring around you shows how far you can jump with the fuel aboard (fainter: a full tank). 'l monitor' with a handheld hyperlane status monitor (Lodestar station, Eeropha) fills them in. 'lanes' lists them.

New: Utilities > Ship Stats. Every ship stat with what one point (or +5, +10, +20) is worth: seconds off a jump, faster in and out, range, hull, weapons fire rate, plus the quota and credit cost. Works for any ship you've done 'info' on, so you can show customers what an upgrade buys them.

Fixed: 'radar' was sent twice after every launch and every jump (Autoflight sent one even when it wasn't flying). Blocked hyperspace routes ('interference') are remembered and flagged in Trade. Ship DB lookups now wait for the quiet minutes in hyperspace during Auto Cargo, instead of sending the dockworkers away.

New: Auto Cargo. In Trade, click 'auto cargo' on any route, choose the planet you start on and your cargo ship (Utilities > Auto Cargo), stand on that pad outside the ship and press START. Each stop it checks the hold (listcargo), sells what it brought, buys the next cargo (fewer units if you can't afford a full hold), boards, closes the hatch, walks to the cockpit, flies, lands, walks out, closes the hatch behind you and refuels to full. Watch the screen while it runs (HELP BOTTING). Help > Guides > Auto Cargo.

Ships you have clan or owner rights to just open; a ship someone lent you opens with its hatch code (type it once in the code box). The walk to the cockpit is built in per ship class (YT-1000, Flashfire); others can be added with 'autocargo class'.
Trade: 'Scan all planets' now asks every planet at once instead of one every 5 seconds (any that fail are asked again once).

Trade: profits are now after the selling planet's tax, permits you buy are remembered (the route stops saying 'permit'), and the credits-per-hour figures switch to real timings as soon as Auto Cargo has flown a leg.

New: Action timer. In the bottom-right corner of the main window a bar fills up while something takes time (two at once stack, each with its name and time above it): loading or unloading cargo, launching, jump calculations, hyperspace (it follows the game's countdown), landing, turbolifts, locateship. It learns how long each one really takes (amber = still a guess, green = learned). 'atimer' lists them, 'atimer off' hides it.

Landing: Auto Cargo picks a pad at random among a planet's allowed ones each time (Arkania: Alpha or Beta, Bespin: Platform 327 or 401, Naboo: Theed only), never a garage or a clan pad, and tries the next if one refuses. New planets: their first pad, then the next. Set your own: 'pads use <planet> = <pad>, <pad>', 'pads avoid <planet> = <pad>'.
Toolbar panels (Datapad, Help, Trade, Utilities...) now open and close instantly instead of sliding in: snappier, and no more half-finished slides.

Turbolifts: the Cloud City lifts on Bespin work now (their directory has a blank line that cut the reading short; floors 221, 317, 327 and 401 are built in), and a bug that saved nonsense floor rooms is fixed.

New: Turbolift panel. Inside a turbolift an elevator panel slides in beside the map and chat: the lift's directory on a screen and round floor buttons. Click one to ride there. It already knows the Merr-Sonn, Ryloth City, East Hangar and Academy lifts; any other lift is learned the first time you look at its panel, plate or directory. Help > Guides > Turbolifts.

The panel shows your CURRENT FLOOR like a real lift: learned when the doors open after a ride, and from the room you walk in from (each room beside a lift belongs to a floor; it learns more every time you step out).

Ship maps: the YT-1000 picture is bigger and lined up with its rooms (the cockpit corridor and cockpit were floating above the ship), and its cockpit, one floor up, has its own picture: go up and the map shows the cockpit pod instead of an empty background. Pictures now update themselves on your map when a new version changes them.

Ships: 'stat' aboard a ship is now kept too (hull, shields, fuel, ammo, cargo), next to its 'info'. Both show on the ship's Storage page and in 'shipdb <ship>' (access codes hidden until you click show codes).
Accent: a grumble like ", eh" now only comes at the end of a sentence, never in the middle of one ("a betta deal, eh dan dat" was the old way). An "eh" you type yourself is always kept.
Fixed: the accent now works on 'clan <text>' (the short way to type clantalk), not just 'clantalk'.
Fixed: an accent phrase's result is no longer changed again word by word (a phrase that gave "no have" could come out as "nah have").
Accent: 'accent list' shows every word and phrase your accent uses (your style's and your own), and how often the sometimes-changes happen.

Accent now starts blank for everyone: build your character's own voice with 'accent swap <word> = <new>' and 'accent phrase <words> = <new>', try it with 'accent test <text>', then 'accent on'. (The Toydarian voice from 1.13.0 was the owner's own and isn't included any more.) Help > Guides > Accent.

Accent: 'accent review' lists the sentences that went out exactly as you typed them, so missing words are easy to spot. What you say is kept as typed and as sent in your own omi_accent_log.txt (never shared).

New: Accent. Your character's way of talking goes on what you say in character (say, sayto, whisper, CommNet, clan, broadcast, hails, quoted speech in emotes). Built in: a Watto-like Toydarian voice ('That sounds exciting' -> 'Dat sounds excitin''). Off until you type 'accent on'; 'accent test <text>' shows it first, '!' before a line sends it as typed. Help > Guides > Accent.

Ship DB: back at a pad you've seen before, it lists every ship that arrived since your last visit: NEW if you've never seen it anywhere, otherwise its owner (and their clan) and where it was last seen, with a [locate] link to look it up straight away. The first visit to a pad is still just one line.

Ark Run: lommite now digs 10 rooms along the tunnel through Mount Ravkin (it was 2). With lommite switched on, the run walks the whole tunnel from the west end out to the Mining Village Entrance, digging as it goes: only 6 more commands than the normal loop. Still off by default (Utilities > Ark Run).

Fixed: a 'dub' or 'greet' that fails ("They aren't here.") is no longer saved in your memory log, however often you retry it. Lines that just happened to arrive meanwhile (like an interrupted study) are left out of memory records too.

Journal: CommNet channels have names. General (0), Confederacy (1), Republic (1024), Durafly (455) and Merr-Sonn (5555) each get their own entry under Recordings; frequencies without a name sit under 'Other frequencies'.
Name any channel as you learn whose it is: 'name this channel' on its page, or 'journal freq <number> = <name>'. Your names stay on your computer.
People pages and dossiers say where someone was heard: 'General 12, Republic 3, clan comms 5, in person 2'.
Fixed: a 'locateship' you type yourself is now kept too (before, only 'shipdb locate' runs were), so the owner's dossier gets the ship.
Dossiers: anyone who talks on your clan comms gets their clan, division and rank filled in (only members can talk there). Your old clan-comm recordings are read once too.

Dossiers: clan members you only know by a description ('A Human male') are listed on the Dossiers home page under UNNAMED, with their race, rank and last lines. Click 'name them' once you know who it is.
Fixed: a dossier showed only the name and nothing else (one of its links was missing the hover text Mudlet requires). Every panel's links now always have one.
Fixed: 'lookup' now reads any databank file, however the player laid it out (NAME: / SPECIES: / ALLEGIANCE: style too), and keeps the whole file in the dossier.
Guides: Help (toolbar) now starts with OMILOTJ GUIDES, a short how-to page for every tool we've built. Type 'guide' to open them, or 'guide <word>' (guide dossiers, guide arkrun, guide shipdb...).

Dossiers fill themselves in with what the game tells you outright: someone introducing themself (or you to them), a dub, 'lookup' with a datapad (race, sex, level, clan and rank, and the whole databank file), 'locateship' owners (the ship goes into their file), 'memory' (names and how they look), and every name the Journal knows. Each file gets a contact log of when and where you met.

Ship DB notes ships in space too: the ones you see out of the cockpit while flying (the bright yellow list) and every ship on 'radar', with the system and the planet they were near. New ones join the list for 'shipdb locate'.
The chat wrap fix from 1.8.1 really is in this one (the 1.8.1 download went out without it).

Fixed: chat tabs could wrap lines far too short (a few words per line in a wide box) when the chat's width was measured while Mudlet was still opening. The wrap now follows the chat box's real width (new lines; older lines keep their wrapping).

Dossiers (new toolbar button): your own file on each person, like a records database. Clan, rank, profession, who they work for, race, base, plus lists of other names, disguises you've seen, restrung armor looks, ships, shops and notes. You fill it in as you work things out; nothing fills itself in.
Every entry remembers when you wrote it and where you were, and is tagged IC (learned in play), PUB (public) or OOC (don't use it in character). Changing someone's clan keeps the old one as history.

Clues next to what you wrote: where the Ship DB saw each of their ships (which pads), the shop catalog's stock, and what your recordings hold (lines by or about them, also under each disguise, memory notes, thoughts).

Ship DB lookups work now: it reads the real locateship answer (owner, dock, planet), waits for each lookup to finish before starting the next (sending the next one early cut every lookup off), and tries again after 'no record found' or an interruption. Ships whose earlier lookups got nothing are looked up again by 'shipdb locate'.

Search finds people by any ship, disguise, name or note. 'dossier <name> ship = <ship>' adds things from the command line; Journal person pages get an 'open dossier' link. Dossiers stay on your PC: they're never shared.
Fixed: the Utilities button didn't open on screens where the toolbar is narrow (the version number sat on top of it). The buttons now shrink to fit.
Fixed: a long hail could get the next game message stuck onto its end in the hail window (like 'You are too close to ... to make the jump to lightspeed!').
Fixed: toolbar buttons often needed two or three clicks. A click while a panel is still sliding now waits its turn instead of being ignored, and the button lights up the moment you click it.

Ark Run: choose what to gather (crate, wireless, test results, crystal chips, frozen organisms, the tunnel credit, Arkanian diamonds, blue diamonds, lommite) in Utilities > Ark Run or with 'arkrun gather <kind> on|off'. Start takes the shortest loop for what's switched on.
Ark Run: type your locker number in the box on the Ark Run page (or 'arkrun locker <n>'). Each player sets their own; too-heavy pickups go there and the pickaxe comes from it.
Not gathering crates: the run goes straight away and, after the loop, waits for the city's reset line before going again.
Ship maps mark the rooms that matter: cockpits yellow 'C', turrets red 'T', engine rooms green 'E' (rooms the game tags [ENGINE], or with Engine in the name).
Every ship already on your map gets marked when Mudlet starts, and every ship of a class shares the marks.
Clan private datanet: 'dncrawl MS private' (any clan you belong to) also saves the members-only pages, kept apart in their own folder and marked with the character who read them.
Datapad: members-only pages show in orange under their clan, in a MEMBERS ONLY section below the public pages.
Ark Run: no more lommite digging in the tunnel (the blue diamond digs stay), and after emptying your pockets into the locker it takes your comlinks back out, so you can still hear and talk.
Ship pictures: the Naboo N-1 Starfighter now has one under its map, and the LAAT/s Gunship's picture shows up (its name was wrong).

Ship DB: every ship you pass (pads, hangars, the view from your cockpit) is noted quietly with where it was seen. 'shipdb locate' (or Utilities > Ship DB) runs locateship on the new ones, from anywhere; owners are kept as a history, so a sold ship shows who had it before. 'shipdb owner <name>' lists what someone owns.
Fixed: in space the ship bar flickered over the bottom of the game text (and its scrollbar) about once a second.

Themes: framed map, chat, bottom and ship bars plus matching toolbar colours, one look per class (combat, piloting, engineering, bounty hunting, smuggling, leadership, espionage, slicer, medical, science, force) or the plain datapad look.
The theme follows your main class (the cyan one in 'score' or 'levels'); pick any other with 'theme <name>' or Utilities > Themes. The ship bar's frame only shows while you're in a ship.
Click the version number on the toolbar: what's new, and an instant check for updates.
Ship pictures on the map: a top-down drawing of the ship sits under its map, lined up with the rooms (you see the Flashfire with you in its cockpit).
Drawn so far: Flashfire, Star Commuter shuttle, JumpMaster 5000, YT-1000, Star Galleon, LAAT/s, Vigo gunship. 'shipmap art nudge <east> <north>' fine-tunes the spot.
Aboard a ship the map zooms in so the ship fills it, and zooms back out when you leave ('shipmap zoom off' to stop it, 'shipmap zoom <n>' for n rooms across).
Recordings skip the whole login screen (account, passwords, character list): they start right after your last password, at the Message of the Day or 'Reconnecting'.
Recording (rec) starts by itself every time Mudlet starts; 'rec off' stops it until the next start. Your login is never recorded.
Update check the moment you log in (your first room in the game), then every 15 minutes from there.
Update window: the buttons show each step (Downloading... / Installing... / Updated), extra clicks are ignored while it works, and it closes by itself when done.
Buttons with nothing to do are greyed out instead of disappearing; the map asks for a second click before it replaces yours.
Updates are also checked when you connect and every 15 minutes, not only when Mudlet starts. 'Later' means no reminder for that version until you restart Mudlet.
Ship map areas are named after the ship's class ('Star Commuter 2000 Transport'), not each ship: one area per class, all its ships share it.
Old per-ship areas (PUB04, PUB10, PUB29, your own ships) are folded into their class areas by themselves when Mudlet loads.
A class's blueprint is learned from the map as soon as you board one, even right after Mudlet starts.
Ship maps: one blueprint per ship class. Board any ship of a mapped class (every Star Commuter shuttle, every Flashfire) and its whole map is drawn at once.
Map a new class once (board, 'map start', walk it, leave) and it works in every ship of that class. Blueprints come with updates.
Utilities > Ship Maps lists the blueprints; 'shipmap' does the same in the main window.
Version numbers: shown on the toolbar (click for this list).
Updates from inside Mudlet: new versions and maps are offered in a pop-up when the profile loads ('omiupdate' checks now). This is the last package you install by hand.
Utilities button: Fly Loop (your own ship, any two planets, landing pads), Landing Pads list, Ark Run controls.
Hail pop-up: ship hails open a movable window in the middle of the screen; reply from it. 'hails' opens it.
Bank: 'bank list' now works with any prompt (it waited for one particular prompt before).
Landing pads are learned whenever you type 'land <planet>' in orbit without a pad ('pads' lists them).
